_doc: Atomic Jev (TypeSafe System One, model jev-latest) questions used by tools/jev.py. {placeholders} are filled in code. Types: choice, score (criteria = rubric levels from 0), noul (yes/no probability), box (bounding box in the state image).

pick.instructions: Pick the best topic for a YouTube Short on a channel whose motto is 'True mysteries science can't fully explain, in under 60 seconds'. Prefer: UFO/radar/signals with an official record or a hard number; aviation or maritime vanishings with a physical clue; mass environmental anomalies with one hard number. Prefer a strong frame-one hook, verified sources, nothing graphic or exploitative.

hook.instructions: How strong is the FIRST line as a scroll-stopping hook for a mystery Short? A strong hook states an exact number or a named subject, plus impossible physical evidence, plus a concrete setting, inside 2.5 seconds, with no date/place preamble and no vague 'something'.
criteria: 3: named subject and a strange detail
4: number or name + impossible evidence + setting, instantly gripping

pacing.instructions: Rate the pacing of this ~50-second narration: a new concrete reveal every 10-12 seconds, a 'But...' twist around 15-18 seconds, no filler, wrap-up or padding.
criteria: 4: relentless, every line adds a new concrete fact

payoff.instructions: Rate the ending: the last line should deliver the strongest unexplained detail and end on 'Nobody explained it.', looping back to the hook, with no moral and no call to action.
criteria: 4: chilling payoff that loops straight back to line one

claim.instructions: Is every factual claim in this narration line ({line}) supported by the fact pack in the state? Answer no if a number, name, date or event in the line is missing from or contradicts the fact pack.

criteria.true: Every claim in the line is supported by the fact pack.
criteria.false: At least one claim is unsupported or contradicted.

title.instructions: Which YouTube Shorts title will earn the most clicks while staying truthful? Best: 38-48 characters before ' #shorts', two clauses 'Fact. Twist.', a concrete number or object, never the answer, never '| Case Name'.

thumb.instructions: Which 2-5 word on-screen hook text for frame 0 would stop a scroller fastest for this story, while staying truthful?

narrator.instructions: Two Shorts are made today and the narrators must alternate: one gets the male narrator, the other the female narrator. Which assignment suits the two stories better?

palette.instructions: Which muted caption palette best suits this story's mood and its night-time 3D plates while staying readable over them?

bed.instructions: Which synthesized sound bed suits this story (no music tracks are allowed)?

criteria.heartbeat: low drone plus a heartbeat that accelerates into the final reveal (tension, danger, vanishings)
criteria.drone: low drone only, colder and quieter (space, signals, archaeology, eerie calm)

readable.instructions: Is this frame from a vertical mystery Short well exposed (not too dark, not blown out) and is all on-screen text clearly readable at phone size?

criteria.true: Well exposed and every text element is readable.
criteria.false: Too dark, blown out, or some text is hard to read.

caption_box.instructions: Locate all on-screen caption and headline text in this frame (one box around all text).

interest.instructions: How visually interesting is this frame as a still from a cinematic 3D mystery Short?

post.instructions: Given the machine QA metrics and the Jev scores in the state, should this Short be posted to a channel that values quality? Answer no if any hard metric failed, the hook is weak, facts are unsupported, or several frames are unreadable or have text outside the safe area.
